findings.title: The grant shortcut length is not constrained to the decoder's fixed format
findings.body: The decoder requires exactly six context characters and reads the grant shortcut from the last two, but `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not enforce a two-character value and its Javadoc says shortcuts are usually three characters. A custom grant factory returning a three-character shortcut will produce token IDs that this decoder rejects, so encoding and decoding do not round-trip for supported providers. Require and validate exactly two characters, or make the format support variable-length shortcuts.

findings.title: The access-token event matcher never checks the expected grant shortcut
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies positions 4–5, but this matcher extracts positions 3–4 and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut. Consequently it accepts a well-formed UUID token ID regardless of its grant type, so event tests cannot catch incorrect grant metadata. Compare the correct two-character segment and reject IDs whose segment differs from the expected shortcut.

findings.title: The constructor checks grantType twice and allows a null raw token ID
findings.body: This second `requireNonNull` checks `grantType` again instead of checking `rawTokenId`. Passing a null raw ID therefore succeeds, and `encodeTokenId` concatenates it as the literal string `null`, producing an ID that no longer represents the supplied context. Validate `rawTokenId` here.
